messages:
Sam: heads-up — p99 for /v1/generate just had a ~700ms jump on the latency dashboard when the rollout weight shifted. p50/p95 look fine. anyone else seeing a weird non-smooth bump?

Kai: same. only for that endpoint and only right after the routing policy changed (weighted -> 70/30). looks like a discrete gap rather than gradual drift. :thinking:

Nina: can you paste the dashboard query you ran? might be windowing.

Sam: sure — this is the rollup query we use in the console:

```sql
-- console rollup with decaying window
SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 50) AS p50, percentile(latency_ms, 95) AS p95, percentile(latency_ms, 99) AS p99
FROM request_rollups
WHERE endpoint = '/v1/generate'
GROUP BY time(1m)
WINDOW decaying(30m)
```

Sam: I also ran a quick sim locally where I drop a single 2s tail sample and p99 snaps down immediately, so behavior matches a sample leaving the decaying window.

Jem: important distinction: decaying windows intentionally reduce weight on older samples, but should produce smooth transitions. a sharp jump suggests either bucket boundary alignment or merge/retention bug. could be rollup shard merging at different alignment rounds.

Kai: I dug into the rollup code — merging intervals uses floor(ts / rollup_interval) * rollup_interval. If the routing change triggers an out-of-order write with an older ts, it might push a heavy tail into a recent bucket then remove it on the next merge. messy.

Nina: do we have waveform of sample counts? if p99 moves but counts drop to 0 for the tail bucket, that's a signal it's leaving the window vs being resampled.

Sam: pasted a tiny log from my sim:

```
[11:12:03] ingest: sample {ts: 2258879990, latency_ms: 2020, route: canary}
[11:12:04] rollup-merge shard-7: bucket 2258879940-2258879999: count=1 p99=2020
[11:13:00] routing-change: canary weight -> 70%
[11:13:15] rollup-merge shard-7: bucket 2258879940-2258879999: dropped (age > decay window)
[11:13:15] dashboard: p99 drop 2020 -> 340
```

Jem: that log is exactly the symptom. two follow-ups: 1) ensure out-of-order writes respect bucket assignment and 2) make decay function continuous across merge boundaries (interpolate weights at bucket edges).

Kai: agree. also think we should annotate dashboard when rollout weights change so ops can correlate spikes to policy updates instead of chasing infra.

telemetry-bot: note created — INFR-472: investigate decaying-window percentile discontinuities (assignee: Jem) :white_check_mark:

Sam: nice. actionables:
- Jem to investigate merge/decay math + unit test for boundary case (INFR-472)
- Kai to add dashboard annotation for routing policy updates and a tooltip explaining decaying-window semantics
- Nina to add a small sampling-waveform panel (count + max) next to p99 so spikes are easier to interpret

deploy-bot: rollout to canary complete for routing policy change (version v2.4.1) :rocket:

Nina: I'll add the waveform panel and a short blurb in the dashboard docs. marking this thread for follow-up once Jem has a patch. :eyes:

Sam: thanks all — keeping an eye. if anyone sees a similar jump on other endpoints please ping @oncall.
